daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The DPR and government have reached agreement on converting part-time PPPK teachers to full-time status beginning in 2027, a move that Finance Minister Sri Mulyani assured would not threaten fiscal sustainability. The policy shift represents a significant employment change for thousands of contract teachers across Indonesia. The Finance Minister emphasized the government's capacity to absorb the additional fiscal burden without compromising budget health.

  • A DPR Commission XIII leader has expressed support for limited dual citizenship, presenting arguments in favor of the proposed policy change.
  • The Golkar party raised Rp 4 billion from its cadres to support earthquake victims in East Nusa Tenggara.
  • The Social Affairs Ministry has partnered with the police to follow up on findings that some social assistance recipients have been using funds for online gambling.
  • Social Affairs Minister Gus Ipul warned that social assistance is for needs, not for online gambling.
  • Legal Affairs Minister Yusril has formed a team to formulate PT Timah's purchasing policy from local communities in East Belitung, and separately assured that the state tin company would continue purchasing from residents there.
  • President Prabowo's potential visit to earthquake-hit NTT is still being planned, according to a minister.
  • The Agriculture Ministry has dismissed 14 officials over corruption allegations.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's ambassador to Japan has presented credentials to the Japanese Emperor, formalizing diplomatic representation. This ceremonial milestone marks the formal beginning of the new ambassador's tenure in Tokyo. Meanwhile, Indonesia and China are strengthening strategic partnership through the Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue and 2+2 Dialogue mechanisms.

  • The Indonesian Embassy in Cambodia has appreciated Cambodian authorities' support in handling online scam operations affecting Indonesian citizens.
  • The Indonesian Consulate in Cape Town has opened Indonesian language classes (BIPA) as interest in the language grows in South Africa.
  • Senior officials from APEC member countries discussed mental health and disaster mitigation issues at a regional meeting.
  • A TNI soldier, Pratu Rizki Kurniawan, was killed by OPM gunfire during Indonesia's 81st Independence Day ceremony in Mimika, with two other soldiers wounded.
  • The TNI has accelerated its earthquake response in NTT, moving from evacuation to establishing field kitchens for survivors.

Other

Minister Yusril conveyed President Prabowo's directive that Indonesia must determine global tin prices, signaling an assertive stance on the commodity market given Indonesia's position as a major producer. The instruction reflects the government's ambition to leverage Indonesia's tin reserves for greater market influence. This policy direction comes amid ongoing discussions over PT Timah's role in the domestic tin sector.

  • The Attorney General's Office is investigating staff and advisors to the Attorney General in connection with the MBG governance case, and separately examined directors of PT BUIL and PT JPP over a West Kalimantan bauxite mining case.
  • The KPK alleges that singer Bebizie received money from coal mining interests in Kutai Kartanegara, not singing fees.
  • Police seized a Tanzania-flagged vessel carrying 1.6 tons of liquid methamphetamine in Bengkalis waters.
  • Bareskrim raided a shophouse in North Jakarta that served as a gold transaction and processing center, part of a broader investigation into gold smuggling to Dubai using gel concealed in undergarments.
  • Danantara's leadership has commented on the fate of Waskita shares under the state holding company.
